content:
iguana’s reflection and serialization support needs to be extended and tightened for several test-visible cases across JSON, XML, protobuf, CMake, and formatting validation.

CMake should expose a build option `ENABLE_CXX26_REFLECTION` that, when enabled with a compiler supporting GCC-style C++26 static reflection, builds and runs `_cpp26` variants of the existing tests using `-std=gnu++26 -freflection`. These test executables must be registered with CTest and must be able to find the correct runtime `libstdc++` when executed. Tests that read files from the source tree, such as `test_json_files` and `test_github_events`, should have their CTest working directory set to the repository’s `test` directory so they can locate `data/` consistently, including inside GitHub Actions containers.

The C++26 reflection path should support annotations for reflected names and skipped members. A struct annotated with `ylt::reflection::reflect26::struct_name<"...">` should use that name where the serialized format has a root/type name, such as XML. A field annotated with `ylt::reflection::reflect26::field_name<"...">` should use the annotated name for JSON, XML, YAML, and protobuf schema generation and should also accept that name on input. A field annotated with `ylt::reflection::reflect26::skip_field{}` should be excluded from the reflected member list and from serialization/deserialization. Base classes annotated with `skip_base` should be excluded from recursive member collection.

JSON reflection should also honor alias metadata supplied without the normal reflection macro. For a C++20 type that provides `get_alias_field_names(T*)` returning `std::array` of `ylt::reflection::field_alias_t`, JSON output should use those aliases and JSON input should map those alias names back to the corresponding fields. For example, a type with fields `x` and `y` and aliases `"X"` and `"Y"` should serialize to `{"X":1,"Y":2}` and deserialize from `{"Y":4,"X":3}` into `x == 3` and `y == 4`.

XML required-field validation must match exact field names. If a struct has fields `id` and `identifier`, and only `id` is marked required via `REQUIRED(type, id)` or via the C++26 annotation `[[= iguana::xml_required{}]]`, then an XML document containing only `<identifier>...</identifier>` must still be rejected as missing the required `id` field. C++26 XML name annotations must also be honored: annotated struct names should control the XML root element, annotated field names should control element names, and `xml_required` should enforce presence using the effective serialized field name.

Protobuf support should cover proto3 binary wire behavior needed for interoperability and conformance-style testing. The public API should support explicit protobuf metadata both through helper descriptors returned by `get_members_impl(T*)` and through C++26 annotations. The helper API should include `pb_members(...)`, `pb_field<&T::field, N>("name")`, `pb_bytes_field`, `pb_zigzag_field`, `pb_fixed_field`, `pb_optional_field`, `pb_timestamp_field`/`as_timestamp_field`, `pb_duration_field`/`as_duration_field`, `pb_oneof_field<&T::field, Ns...>("name")`, `pb_unknown_fields_field`, and `pb_field_ex` with combinable options such as `pb_bytes`, `pb_zigzag`, `pb_fixed`, `pb_optional`, `pb_as_timestamp`/`as_timestamp`, and `pb_as_duration`/`as_duration`. The C++26 annotation equivalents should include `[[= iguana::pb_field(N)]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_bytes]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_zigzag]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_fixed]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_optional]]`, `[[= iguana::pb_oneof<N...>]]` or `[[= iguana::oneof<N...>]]`, `[[= iguana::as_timestamp]]` or `[[= iguana::pb_as_timestamp]]`, `[[= iguana::as_duration]]` or `[[= iguana::pb_as_duration]]`, and `[[= iguana::pb_unknown_fields]]`.

Explicit protobuf field numbers must be validated according to proto3 rules: valid field numbers are in `[1, 2^29 - 1]`, excluding the reserved range `[19000, 19999]`. The default field-number assignment should remain based on member order when no explicit field number is supplied. `to_proto<T>(std::string&, "package")` should generate a proto3 schema view that reflects the selected field names, field numbers, and wire-related metadata.

The protobuf reader and writer should handle proto3 binary wire cases including varint, fixed32/fixed64, length-delimited strings and bytes, signed zigzag fields, explicit optional presence, oneof fields represented by `std::variant<std::monostate, ...>`, `google.protobuf.Timestamp` and `google.protobuf.Duration` mapped to chrono types, and unknown field preservation when a message declares a `std::string` unknown-field storage member. Repeated primitive fields should be readable from packed, unpacked, multiple packed chunks, and mixed encodings; serialization should emit packed encoding according to proto3 defaults. Unknown fields, including unknown groups, must be skipped safely without unbounded recursion, and preserved unknown wire bytes should be written back unchanged when an unknown-field storage member is present.

A protobuf conformance testee executable named `iguana_conformance` should be buildable and usable with the official `conformance_test_runner`. It should support the proto3 binary/protobuf-output subset and skip unsupported categories such as JSON, text format, proto2, and non-protobuf output rather than failing unexpectedly. CMake should allow registering this with `PROTOBUF_CONFORMANCE_RUNNER` so it can be run via CTest using `--enforce_recommended`.

The clang-format check used by CI should be reproducible with clang-format 18. Provide a script `scripts/check-clang-format.sh` that accepts an optional base ref, defaults to `HEAD`, uses `clang-format-18` and `git-clang-format-18` by default, allows overriding them through `CLANG_FORMAT` and `GIT_CLANG_FORMAT`, reports missing tools with clear errors such as `error: clang-format-18 not found; install clang-format-18 or set CLANG_FORMAT.`, and fails with the existing message `The diff you sent is not formatted correctly.` followed by the suggested diff when formatting changes are required.

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
